recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed unless a future work group decision changes CodeableReference profiling or validator behavior.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-core issue asking whether CodeableReference binding and targetProfile constraints may also be placed directly on CodeableReference.concept or CodeableReference.reference; the final decision was that profiles SHALL NOT do so and validators should enforce the rule where possible.
initial_application: Jira comments identify master commit bb07b227109ce945918994d616a37171b3ba46f2 and R4B commit e54acba3221b3015925ae860c64bc41966700740 as the application. The master commit added StructureDefinition constraints sdf-24 and sdf-25 to prohibit targetProfile on CodeableReference.reference and binding on CodeableReference.concept.
additional_context: Current build-scoped source also contains CodeableReference prose in source/references.html that maps top-level targetProfile and binding constraints to reference and concept respectively and states that those constraints SHALL NOT be specified on the child elements. Later related combined-branch reconciliations for FHIR-37761, FHIR-39176, FHIR-38957, FHIR-40955, and FHIR-41852 preserve or clarify the same policy; Confluence minutes confirm the original vote; Zulip evidence did not reveal a reversal.
reconciliation: No source change was made because active source already contains both the datatype declaration and the validator-facing StructureDefinition constraints required by the issue.
